req_desc:
Run manifest and health
`/app/run.json` declares the install, build and serve commands and the served app answers the health check, both as stated in Deployment.

Seeded sign-in and roles
Every seeded person signs in with their email and the seed password, lands on their role's home screen and can call only the endpoints API grants that role.

One error shape and order
Every API error uses the one error body and the one precedence order stated in API.

Server boundary
The server enforces the origin, body-size and never-served rules in Server boundary and keeps serving when Kill Bill, MinIO or Mailpit is unreachable at boot.

Configuration from environment
Every service URL and credential is read at start from the environment variables in Configuration and secrets and is never hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Three viewports without overflow
At 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 every screen follows Screens and layout with no horizontal page scroll, and every job row shows its status label and seat counter within the leftmost area stated there.

Ruled dispatch look
Every screen reads as a light, ruled dispatch board with the colour roles, type pairing, compact density and grid described in Visual design.

Motion timing and reduced motion
Panels, fills and feedback move only as timed in Motion and effects, nothing loops for decoration, and a reduced-motion preference swaps every movement for its stated substitute.

Keyboard and focus
Every public control is reachable by Tab in reading order with a visible focus ring, and Escape closes the job detail pane or the cancel dialog and returns focus to the control that opened it.

Draft requests
A client scheduler creates and edits draft requests for their own organisation with the fields and validation in API.

Start times in agency time
Start times are entered and shown in the agency's time zone whatever the browser's zone, with skipped and repeated clock-change hours handled as stated in Business rules.

Submit opens seats
Submitting a draft moves it to submitted and opens seats by the team-size rule in Business rules.

Client request journey
A client scheduler signs in, fills in New request, saves a draft, submits it and sees the request detail with its open seats and the Open seat label.

Team size and rotation settings
A coordinator overrides a request's team size with a recorded reason and sets its rotation interval, within the limits in Business rules.

Open-seat broadcast
Broadcasting a request emails each eligible, free interpreter once with only the facts listed in Services, never the private consumer details named in Business rules.

Coordinator staffing journey
A coordinator opens a job from the week board, sets its rotation interval, broadcasts its open seats and sees the sent count in the Job status region.

Exactly one claim wins
When interpreters claim the same open seat at once, exactly one gets the confirmation, every other gets seat_taken with no email, and every attempt is written to the request history.

Staffing emails
Winning a seat emails the winner and any confirmed teammate, and a request becoming staffed emails its client scheduler, as listed in Services.

Interpreter claim journey
An interpreter signs in, opens a job from Open seats, claims a seat, sees the braid fill and then sees the consumer name and notes in the job detail.

Credential valid on the job date
Only an interpreter whose required credential is verified and unexpired on the job's date sees the seat in Open seats or can claim it; others get credential_invalid.

No overlapping seats
An interpreter never holds two confirmed seats whose time windows overlap; the later claim gets schedule_conflict.

Staffing status from seats
A request's status follows its confirmed seats after every claim and team-size change, as defined in Business rules.

Fields by role
Each API response carries only the fields API publishes for the caller's role, so a client scheduler sees an interpreter's display name and credential badges and never their phone, home area or pay rate.

Organisation isolation
A client scheduler sees only their own organisation's requests, seats and invoices in every list, search and export, and another organisation's id answers the same 404 as an id that does not exist.

Week board rows
The coordinator's week board lists the week's jobs by day with time, reference, organisation, status label and seat counter, an open-seat filter and week navigation, refreshing as stated in Interactions.

Status beyond colour
Open, half-staffed and staffed jobs differ by hatch pattern and text label as well as colour, at the contrast stated in Feedback states.

Braid lanes and segments
Job detail draws the rotation braid as one lane per seat, split into rotation segments with alternating active role, crossover diagonals and hatched open segments named as in Public screens and controls.

Playhead and readout
The braid's playhead moves from 0 to the job length by drag or keyboard, and the Rotation readout names the clock time and the active and support seats.

Fill only after confirmation
A seat's segments fill one by one in start-time order only after the server confirms the claim, and a lost claim keeps the hatching and announces the seat-taken copy.

Braid without motion
With reduced motion requested the braid fills instantly and draws crossovers without animation, while the playhead, keyboard steps, readout and Rotation table work unchanged.

Braid craft
The braid reads as two interlocking lanes whose active band visibly crosses over at each boundary, with open stretches distinct from staffed ones at first look.

Certificate upload limits
An interpreter uploads a certificate within the type and size limits in Server boundary, with type judged by the file's content.

Private certificate files
Certificate files live privately in MinIO under the key pattern in Services and reach only coordinators through the short-lived link in API.

Verification and expiry
A coordinator verifies an uploaded certificate with its expiry date, and the credential reads as expired once that date has passed in agency time.

Storage outage
When MinIO is unreachable, uploads and file links fail with storage_unavailable and the storage copy while every other feature keeps working.

Free-cancellation cutoff
Each request states when free cancellation ends, computed by the agency-time cutoff rule in Business rules so it holds across clock changes.

Fee shown before confirming
Cancelling shows the server's exact fee before the user confirms, and confirming against a fee that has since changed gets fee_changed with the new quote.

Cancellation effects
A confirmed cancellation sets cancelled_early or cancelled_late, frees the seats, records any late fee as one billing charge and sends the cancellation emails in Services.

Completion with actual minutes
A coordinator marks a half-staffed or staffed request completed with its actual minutes.

Exact charge at close
Closing a completed request computes the charge once by the charge rule in Business rules, and the same amount appears in Postgres, the Kill Bill invoice item and the invoice email.

One billing item per charge
Each close or late-cancellation fee becomes exactly one Kill Bill invoice item on the client organisation's account, and the Kill Bill invoice id is stored on the charge.

Invoice pending and recovery
When Kill Bill is unreachable the charge is saved as invoice pending and posts exactly once after Kill Bill returns, without a restart, as qualified in Server boundary.

Idempotent close and cancel
Close and cancel take an Idempotency-Key, replay the stored response for a repeated key and reject a key reused for a different action, as stated in Business rules.

Invoice list, search and export
The billing admin and client schedulers list invoices, search them by reference and export them as CSV with the columns in API.

Billing admin journey
The billing admin signs in, closes a completed request from Ready to close, sees its amount and billing status, and finds it in Invoices and the CSV export.
/app/run.json is valid JSON containing exactly the string keys _schema (value run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve.
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font, each with its version and licence.
Every shipped package (the production tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) is licensed MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0 or 0BSD; bundled fonts are OFL-1.1.
No datastore is used beyond Postgres, Kill Bill and MinIO: no SQLite, Redis, embedded database or certificate files kept on local disk.
The provided service configuration and its seeded development credentials are left unchanged.
Fonts and every other frontend asset are served from the app itself; no page loads anything from a third-party origin at runtime.
/app/package-lock.json is committed and matches package.json.
